_doc: captions.example.json -> copy to scenes/captions.json. ONE source of truth for the burned-in lane AND the sidecar:
node scenes/lib/captions.js scenes/timing_film_data.js scenes/captions.json --out out/caption_groups.json --js scenes/captions_data.js
style:  anchor | broadcast | documentary | keynote | ink | conference | typewriter | clipwipe  (CAP.STYLES; table in references/captions-and-overlays.md)
mode:   default fate of every phrase: rail (verbatim lane) | drop (not shown) | embed (big centred, one caption at a time)
phases: per-phase fate or {fate, style, ink:'dark'|'light'} — e.g. drop the title phase whose words are already the title card
overrides: per-word tweaks keyed by phase + word (+ n-th occurrence): em (accent + weight 700), display (spoken 'twenty three' -> '23'),
drop (filler in a real-audio segment), color / weight / scale (scale <= 1.10 on the rail). No x/y nudges: they break the collision gate.
grouping: optional overrides of the measured defaults (gap 0.35 s, commaGap 0.25 s, maxDur 2.5 s, minWords 2, minDur 0.5 s, lead 0.08 s, tail 0.6 s,
maxWords / maxChars default to the style's tokens; density:true lowers the cap to 2/3/4 words at > 3.5 / > 2.5 words per second)
luma: optional probe result (python gates/overlay_gate.py --probe) {phase: {mean, p95}} -> dark ink on bright screens (> 150), bare light text (< 60), scrim between
Everything here is fictional (Acme, synthetic data). Keep this file in qa.json 'authored' so display substitutions pass the hygiene / over-claims gates.
A phase whose words are already on screen (title card, closing card) is 'drop' - captioning it twice is the text-on-text failure the overlay gate flags.
